chunks: From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Sandal, from Dawood ibn Farqad, who said:

I was sitting in the house of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I looked at a Ra'ibi pigeon cooing for a long time. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) looked at me and said: 'O Dawood! Do you know what this bird is saying?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is supplicating against the killers of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), therefore take it to be in your houses.'

key_terms.الْجَامُورَانِيُّ: Al-Jamourani, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَاعِبِيٍّ: Ra'ibi, a specific breed or type of pigeon
key_terms.يُقَرْقِرُ: Cooing/making the sound of a pigeon

ai.seo_question: What did the pigeon say according to Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia belief in the spiritual awareness of animals, specifically linking the cooing of a 'Raba'i' pigeon to the ongoing supplication against the killers of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Scholars interpret this as a sign of the continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt's legacy in the natural world, encouraging believers to maintain a physical and spiritual connection to the Imams through domesticating these birds. It underscores the concept of *Dua* extending beyond human speech into the created world, reinforcing the emotional and theological bond with the martyrdom of the third Imam.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Jamourany, form Ibn Abu Hamza, from Sandal, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said,

‘I was seated in the house of Abu Abdullahasws, so I looked at an Al-Ra’aiby pigeon cooing for a long time. So Abu Abdullahasws looked at me, so heasws said: ‘O Dawood! Do you know what this bird is saying?’ I said, ‘No, by Allahazwj, may I be sacrificed for youasws’. Heasws said: ‘It is supplicating against the killers of Al-Husaynasws, therefore take it to be in your houses’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Jamuraniy from ibn abu Hamzah from Sandal from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following:

“I once was sitting in the house of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and I looked at a pigeon of Ra’‘ibiy kind (name of a place) that made a long sound. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, looked at me and asked, ‘O Dawud, do you know what this bird says?’ I said, ‘No, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It prays against the people who murdered al- Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, so you must keep it in your homes.’”
